result.title: InfoOrgBench: Can Agents Turn Scattered Information into Coherent Hierarchies?
result.summary: When agents organize records into folders, they may correctly group the excerpts of a design proposal yet place the proposal under the wrong owning group. Existing agent benchmarks do not directly measure such higher-level errors. We introduce InfoOrgBench, a benchmark of 150 tasks in which agents organize scattered records from meeting recaps, issue threads and design proposals into hierarchies. Integrity checks verify that every record is preserved, and a Structure Score measures agreement with the source hierarchy at every level, independent of folder names and order. We evaluate 45 systems that pair nine models with five agent harnesses. The best system scores 83.2 out of 100, but no system exceeds 78 on meeting recaps or issue threads. Model choice affects scores far more than harness choice: model means span about 27 points, whereas the average effect of each harness is below one point. More importantly, parent-level relations have higher error rates than leaf-level relations in all three domains. In design proposals, nearly half of the outputs analyzed by level make exactly this kind of error. These results show that evaluating information organization requires measuring higher-level relations separately from record preservation and local grouping.

AI.brief_summary: InfoOrgBench 提出一个含 150 个任务的基准，让 agent 把散落的会议纪要、issue 与设计提案记录整理成层级结构，并以逐层结构与源层级比对的结构分数、外加完整性检查，评测 45 个模型与框架组合，发现高层父子关系的错误率高于叶层关系。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「逐层评分、区分高层与叶层关系错误」的诊断方式，可能可供核查 LVR 中证据与推理状态的层级化组织及结构化表示评价；但论文本身为纯文本信息组织，与视觉或 latent reasoning 无直接联系，借鉴性需进一步判断。
